questions.question: When parked on the road, how should a motorcycle be positioned?

options.text: At an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb.
Without any wheel or fender touching the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: At an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb.
questions.explanation: A parked motorcycle should be at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb. At least one wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the alcohol is consumed.
How often the person drinks alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person drinks alcohol.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on body weight, the amount of alcohol consumed, and how fast it is consumed. It does not depend on how often someone drinks. Do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: A person is considered intoxicated at a blood alcohol content (BAC) of ____.
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Virginia, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means a person is intoxicated. Intoxicated people cannot legally operate a motor vehicle.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of a motorcycle colliding with other traffic?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where motorcycles and other vehicles have the most conflict. Always be careful when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: An engine will seize because of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Not enough oil.
questions.explanation: Engines seize when oil is low. Without oil, engine parts cannot move smoothly and the engine overheats.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to move.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, move to a different lane to give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: A helmet provides the best protection when it is all of these, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Loose-fitting.
questions.explanation: The best helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards, fits snugly all around, and has no damage such as cracks, loose padding, or torn straps.

questions.question: When passing a truck on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Not move back to your lane until you see the truck's front bumper in your rearview mirror.
Move back to your lane as soon as the truck is behind you.
Move back to your lane when you have enough space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not move back to your lane until you see the truck's front bumper in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing a truck, only return to your lane when you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: When you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do both at the same time.
Do one action, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: When you need to swerve and brake, do them one at a time, not together. Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: Look through turns to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Your rear wheel locks up while you stop on good pavement. What should you do?

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and then quickly apply it again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on good pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop. Your motorcycle can be controlled with a locked rear wheel if it stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what is usually best to do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull to the shoulder and wait for the rain to stop.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Roads are slippery when rain starts, especially in the center of the lane. Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles. The left tire track is often safest.

questions.question: When riding with a group, a staggered formation:

options.text: Should be used at all times.
Should not be used when entering or leaving a highway.
Should be used when riding in curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be used when entering or leaving a highway.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is generally good, but switch to single-file when riding in curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: You reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle. What happens?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Show a narrow view of the road behind you.
Show a wide view of the road behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. They make objects appear farther away than they really are. Take time to get used to convex mirrors if your motorcycle has them.

questions.question: The oily strip down the center of a lane:

options.text: Should only be used if you share the lane with another vehicle.
Provides good traction unless it is raining.
Should be avoided at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides good traction unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily center strip usually provides enough traction for safe riding, except when raining. The strip is usually about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road means:

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers what traffic laws apply in that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcycle responds to turns:
questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to the motorcycle. This extra weight makes the motorcycle slower to speed up, slow down, and turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, do not ride in the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is often the best choice, but this depends on traffic and road conditions.

questions.question: When you are about to pass a vehicle on the left, which part of your lane should you ride in?
questions.correctAnswerText: Left
questions.explanation: When you are about to pass another vehicle on the left, ride in the left part of your lane.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, how should the following distance change?
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, increase your following distance. The trailer adds weight, so your motorcycle will need more time and distance to stop.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head, shoulders, and torso.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: Look through a turn by turning only your head. Keep your shoulders still and your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Small vehicles appear to be ________ and moving slower than they really are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast a small vehicle is going or how far away it is. Do not assume that drivers of larger vehicles can accurately see your speed and distance.
